findings.title: /agent retry on the ticket waits forever on the stopped run's own PR when its create wasn't saved
findings.why: The resume loop asks GitHub for any open PR (no --head, no headRefName) and resumePlan returns 'wait' whenever one exists. When `gh pr create` worked on GitHub but threw before s.pr was saved (the case openPr's new --head lookup was added for), the run stops with s.pr null and its PR open. The owner's /agent retry then finds that same PR, logs 'waits: PR #N is still open' on every tick and never reaches openPr. The 'finished' loop skips it too because s.pr is null, and the ready loop waits on the same PR. The factory stays stuck until someone closes the run's own PR by hand. Fix: look up the open PR with its headRefName and leave out (or adopt) the one on s.branch.

findings.title: stoppedAt and created_at are compared as strings in different ISO formats
findings.why: s.stoppedAt comes from toISOString() (with milliseconds, '…:00.500Z'). GitHub's created_at has none ('…:00Z'). Within the same second 'Z' sorts after '.', so a retry written just before the stop counts as after it. Comparing Date.parse values would fix this.

findings.title: A resumed run's project card stays in Ready
findings.why: stop() moves a run with no PR back to 'Ready'. The resume sets the working label but never calls moveCard(n, 'In Progress') the way a fresh pickup does, so the board shows the ticket as Ready while it is being worked.

findings.title: The stop comment for a run with no PR doesn't mention the new /agent retry on the ticket
findings.why: The retry hint is only added when s.pr is set. A run that stopped before its first push, the only kind #111's resume applies to, doesn't tell the owner that `/agent retry` on the ticket now resumes it.
